Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 57 s. 2023 SEP 2023 ATTY. IAN KENNETH B. LUCERO Provincial Director, DILG-Cebu 2/F East Wing, Legislative Building Cebu Provincial Capitol Compound Escario St., Cebu City Dear Atty. Lucero: This pertains to your letter dated May 26, 2023 requesting the Central Office's opinion and guidance on whether the Governor may fill up a vacancy in the Sangguniang Bayan by appointment without need of a political party nomination. The core of the instant query revolves around the proper procedure in filling up permanent vacancies in the sanggunian under Section 45 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) which reads: SECTION 45. Permanent Vacancies in the Sanggunian. (a) Permanent vacancies in the Sanggunian where automatic successions provided above do not apply shall be filled by appointment in the following manner: (I) The President, through the Executive Secretary, in the case of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan and the Sangguniang Panlungsod of highly urbanized cities and independent component cities; (2) The governor, in the case of the Sangguniang Panlungsod Of component cities and the Sangguniang bayan; (3) The city or municipal Mayor, in the case of Sangguniang Barangay, upon recommendation of the Sangguniang Barangay concemed. (b) Except for the Sangguniang Barangay, only the nominee of the political patty under which the Sanggunian member concerned had been elected and whose elevation to the position next higher in rank created the last vacancy in the Sanggunian shall be appointed in the manner hereinabove provided. The appointee shall come from the same political party as that of the Sanggunian member who caused the vacancy and shall serve the unexpired term of the vacant office. In the appointment herein mentioned, a nomination and a certificate of membership of the appointee from the highest official of the political party concerned are conditions sine qua non, and any appointment without such nomination and certification shall be null and void ab initio and shall be a ground for administrative action against the official responsible therefor. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

(c) In case the permanent vacancy is caused by a Sanggunian member who does not belong to any political party, the local chief executive shall, upon recommendation of the Sanggunian concerned, appoint a qualified person to fill the vacancy. The interpretation you presented is that "when there is a vacancy in case a regular member of the Sangguniang Bayan dies or voluntary resigns, Section 45(b) does not apply." Instead, Section 45(a)(2) which provides that the vacancy in the sangguniang bayan shall be filled by appointment of the governor, will come into force without need of a political party nomination for the replacement of the deceased or resigned SB member You further contended that the present case does not share the same factual background as ruled by the Supreme Court in G.R. No. 141307 entitled "Navarro v. Court of AppealS' as in that case a vacancy was created in the Office of the Mayor following the death of Mayor Cesar Calimlim of Mapandan, Pangasinan. By operation of law, under Section 44 of the LGC, then Vice-Mayor Baltazar Aquino succeeded him. Accordingly, the highest-ranking member of the Sangguniang Bayan, in the person of petitioner Danny B. Tamayo who belonged to the REFORMA-LM political party was elevated to the position of the Vice-Mayor. In that case the Supreme Court held that since a vacancy occurred in the Sangguniang Bayan by the elevation of petitioner Tamayo to the office of the Vice-Mayor, who belonged to REFORMA-LM, to the position of Vice-Mayor, that should be filled up with someone who should belong to the same political party of petitioner Tamayo. Otherwise, REFORMA-LM's representation in the sanggunian would be diminished. However, you advanced the view that "in instances of death or resignation of a regular member of the Sanggunian Bayan, there is no automatic succession or elevation to the position next higher in rank to speak of as all regular sanggunian members are equally occupying the same position regardless of rank." Here, the vacancy created was not caused by elevation to a position next higher in rank but simply due to death or voluntary resignation of the regular SB member and the person who will occupy the slot that the former vacated will neither take a higher position nor elevate to a position next higher in rank. It necessarily follows that the right of the party to be represented in the sanggunian therefore ends with the death or voluntary resignation of the sanggunian member who caused the vacancy there is no need to maintain party representation as enunciated in the Navarro case." With due respect to your position, the Central has a different view. We sustain the applicability of Navarro to the present case. Please be informed that under the LGC, in case of permanent vacancy by reason of death or resignation in the Sangguniang Bayan, the rule on automatic succession by the other sanggunian members shall be applied first. For instance, if the deceased SB Member is ranked number two (2), the third (3rd) ranking SB Member shall first be elevated to the third (3rd) rank, and so on with the remaining SB Members. Thereafter, the resultant vacancy in the last position would call for the application of Section 45 which provides that permanent vacancies in the sangguniang bayan where automatic succession does not apply shall be filled by appointment to be made by the Page 2 of 4

governor. Furthermore, the same provisions stated that the appointee shall come from the same political party as that of the sanggunian member who caused the vacancy and shall serve the unexpired term of the vacant office. Nowhere can we find in pertinent laws or even in jurisprudence that in case of permanent vacancy in the sangguniang bayan under the same circumstances, such party representation is dissolved. In fact, in many jurisprudence decided by the Supreme Court, it maintained the right given to a political party to nominate a replacement where a permanent vacancy occurs in the sanggunian to maintain the party representation as willed by the people in the election. To further bolster this view, we cite the case of Farinas v Barbal where the Supreme Court dealt on the proper interpretation of Section 45. In the said case Carlito B. Domingo was a member of the Sangqunianq Bayan of San Nicolas, Ilocos Norte. On March 24 1994. he resigned after going without leave to the United States. The relevant portion of the decision is quoted hereunder: "In other words, with the exception of the Sangguniang Barangay pars. (a) and (b) must be read as providing for the filling of vacancies in the various Sanggunians when these vacancies are created as a result of the cessation from office (other than expiration of term) of members who belong to political parties. On the other hand, Section 45(c) must be understood as providing for the filling of vacancies created by members who do not belong to any political party. Consequently, Section 45 must be construed to mean that: II. Where the Permanent Vacancy is Caused by a Sanggunian Member belonging to a Political Party A Sangguniang Panlalawigan and Sangguniang Panlungsod of highly urbanized cities and independent component cities - The President, through the Executive Secretary, upon the nomination and certification of the political party to which the member who caused the vacancy belonged, as provided in 45(b). B. Sangguniang Panlungsod of component cities and Sangguniang Bayan - The Governor upon the nomination and certification of the political party to which the member who caused the vacancy belonged, as provided in Sec. 45(b). Where the Vacancy is Caused by a Sanggunian Member Not Belonging to a Political Party A. B. Sangguniang Panlalawigan and Sangguniang Panlungsod of highly urbanized and independent component cities - The President, through the Executive Secretary, upon recommendation of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan or Sangguniang Panlungsod as the case may be. Sangguniang Panlungsod of component cities and Sangguniang Bayan - The Governor upon recommendation of the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang Bayan as the case may be" I G.R. 116763, April 19, 1996. Page 3 of 4

Therefore, applying the foregoing Supreme Court rulings to the case at hand, the person to be appointed to the resultant vacancy in the concerned Sangguniang Bayan should come from the same party affiliation of the deceased or resigned sanggunian member. Further, such appointee must have a nomination and a Certificate of Membership from the highest official of his political party. The highest official shall refer to the Party Chairman. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: OR R. LLAMAS .
